solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swap prize ram for cow?

indicators.note: swap tells us to put the second word's piece before the first's, so the ram comes first

parts.note: a ram is something that butts, so a butter
a cup is a trophy awarded as a prize

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders about trading a prize-winning ram for a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swap' reverses the order of the two pieces as they appear in the clue, so the ram's piece leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttercup is a traditional pet name given to a dairy cow, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Tie up cash within trading group on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the up means the combined letters are read upwards, back to front
within says the money sits inside the trading bloc's letters

parts.note: the EU began as a trading bloc of European nations
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Money is tied up inside a trading bloc that is doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie up two things is to join them together, a close synonym.

clue.text: Earl Grey's on 'Casualty' — poser!

parts.note: Earl Grey is a tea, so Earl Grey's is tea's, giving the letters with the S
ER, the emergency room, is the casualty department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A cup of Earl Grey turns up in the TV hospital drama Casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: Casualty is a long-running BBC hospital drama; here it means the hospital department, the ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling problem, the same as a brainteaser.

clue.text: Country girl (from 'ampshire, reportedly) following career

indicators.note: following says the girl's piece comes after the career piece
reportedly says the pieces are heard rather than read, matching a word spelt differently

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong; said with the next piece it runs into a double S

indicators.note: the dropped aitch of 'ampshire shows a Hampshire voice, which says the girl's word without its H

parts.note: her refers to a girl, and with its aitch dropped it is 'er

explanation.surface: A girl from the Hampshire countryside, with a dropped aitch, is following her career.
explanation.walkthrough: Say rush plus 'er (her with the aitch dropped, Hampshire-style) together, 'rush-'er', and it sounds like the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a nation, the largest country in the world by area.

clue.text: Pia's forgotten petunias, unfortunately not in yet

indicators.note: forgotten says the name's letters are lost from the mix
unfortunately suggests the flowers' letters have come to grief and are jumbled

parts.note: the name Pia, the 's standing for has

explanation.surface: Pia has forgotten to plant her petunias, so they are sadly not in the ground yet.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, I, A from PETUNIAS and rearrange the remaining ETUNS to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unset, like a jelly or a gem, has not yet been fixed into place.

clue.text: Programs for examination set by Thomas and Henry?

parts.note: a search is a close examination
Thomas and Henry are locomotives in the Thomas the Tank Engine children's stories

explanation.surface: Programmes for an exam set by two teachers called Thomas and Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thomas and Henry' look like examiners; they are the tank engines from the Rev. W. Awdry's children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Search engines are software programs that look up information on the internet.

clue.text: A-G on Sky? Rapture!

parts.note: A to G runs through the alphabet up to the seventh letter
the heavens are the sky

explanation.surface: An Attorney-General appears on Sky News, to someone's delight.
explanation.walkthrough: A-G reads like Attorney-General; it is the letters A to G, ending on the seventh.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in seventh heaven is an idiom for a state of complete bliss or ecstasy.

clue.text: Devious medic steals my scheme for two-handed working?

indicators.note: devious means crooked or winding, so the letters take a twisted new order

explanation.surface: A crooked doctor pinches someone's plan for doing things with both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting in tens grew from our ten fingers, two hands' worth, hence the base-ten number scheme.

clue.text: Donna dashed outside shop and weed

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled name goes round the shop
dashed means smashed to pieces, so the name's letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a type of shop

explanation.surface: Donna rushed out of the shop and smoked some weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' makes DANON from DONNA, which goes outside DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a common yellow-flowered plant usually treated as a garden weed.

clue.text: Stand-in's time up inside criminal racket

indicators.note: inside says the turned time piece goes within the jumbled letters
criminal suggests something bent, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A deputy's time is up, caught up in a crooked scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' signals the anagram and 'up' the turnaround of the period of time; 'inside' places that piece just after the first letter of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker government or manager is a temporary stand-in until a permanent one is appointed.

clue.text: Harmonise and transpose reduction of Meyerbeer gavotte

indicators.note: transpose here means turn the letters round, reading them backwards
a reduction of the words is just a part of them, so the letters lie inside

explanation.surface: A musician harmonises and arranges a shortened version of a dance by the composer Meyerbeer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EERGA sit within 'Meyerbeer gavotte'; reading them backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to be in harmony with someone, sharing the same view.

clue.text: Character of Greek articles reaching across time

indicators.note: reaching across says the articles span the time letter, holding it between them

parts.note: the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Greek newspaper articles cover a long stretch of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, a written character.

clue.text: High water, and streak materialising … that's very scary!

indicators.note: materialising means taking a new shape, so the letters re-form into something else

explanation.surface: Floodwater and a streak of something appearing make for a frightening scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A great white is a huge predatory fish, the most feared of all its kind.

clue.text: Goggles worn initially in space against sun

indicators.note: in says the picked letter sits inside the space

parts.note: a gap is a space

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word worn

explanation.surface: Goggles worn in space shield the eyes from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To goggle is to stare open-mouthed, the same as to gawp.

clue.text: Plant acer in different positions around island

indicators.note: around says the jumbled tree goes round the island letter
in different positions says the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener plants maple trees in various spots around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in different positions' turns ACER into ERCA, which goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heathers, a kind of flowering shrub.

clue.text: Squeeze wife in the wood

indicators.note: in says the wife letter goes inside the wood

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: Squeezing one's wife among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a sharp pinch or twist, a kind of squeeze.

clue.text: Diddled about with heart of foliage plant

indicators.note: about says the word is turned round

parts.note: to have someone, or diddle them, is to cheat them

indicators.note: heart of picks the central letters of the word foliage

explanation.surface: Someone cheated around with the centre of a leafy plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns HAD into DAH; the heart of 'foliage' is its middle three letters, LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden flower grown from tubers.

clue.text: Following summons, ambassador gets to struggle

indicators.note: following says the ambassador's letters come after the summons

parts.note: a writ is a legal summons
HE, His Excellency, is the form of address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: After being served a summons, an ambassador has to fight it.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, as when struggling.

clue.text: See 13
Cast, with rod high?

definitions.meaning: the cast of a show is its list of performers, the bill
an angler holding the fishing rod raised has the cord aloft

explanation.surface: An angler casts with the fishing rod held high.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a show is its roster of performers, the same as its billing.

clue.text: Hats off to chap avoiding new complaint

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged
avoiding says the new letter is left out of the man

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Taking hats off to a man who steers clear of a new illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges HATS to ASTH; 'avoiding' removes N from MAN, leaving MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a chronic breathing ailment, and complaint means an illness.

clue.text: See 13
15ed car — with poker?

definitions.meaning: a tweaked car is one modified to run faster
a fire poker just taken from the flames is a heated metal bar

explanation.surface: A souped-up car, along with a fire poker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car modified for speed, and a heated poker is literally such a rod.

clue.text: Net features piece from Timorese author

indicators.note: piece from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer from East Timor contributes a piece about online features.
explanation.definitionFit: A réseau is a mesh or network, such as the ground of lace or a grid of lines.

clue.text: Twig making holes in both ends of stockings

indicators.text: making holes in both ends of
indicators.note: making holes in both ends says the word's first and last letters are knocked out

parts.note: hosiery is the trade word for stockings and tights

explanation.surface: A twig is ripping holes in both ends of a pair of stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose pliant shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: 'Capital' an exemplar of promotion in old capital

indicators.note: in says the promotion goes inside the old capital

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro was the capital of Brazil until 1960
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A capital city's advertising, set in a former capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital is a London commercial station, so it is an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is a broadcaster, an instance of a station on the airwaves.

clue.text: Seek to impress

definitions.meaning: to seek is to pursue or go after
to impress here means to engrave a design into metal

explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to pursue, and also to engrave or emboss metalwork.

clue.text: A royal follower? Crikey, one's nipped George I

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise like crikey

indicators.note: nipped means cut short, leaving only the opening letter of the name George

explanation.surface: Crikey, the dog has bitten King George I!
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen famously kept corgis, dogs that trotted after the monarch.

clue.text: Kindly Arab I dupe vis-a-vis bid?

parts.note: a tender is a bid or offer
the words Arab I dupe have bid as their heart, so with respect to bid they are hearted

explanation.surface: A kind Arab and someone being fooled discuss an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three letters of 'Arab I dupe' are B, I, D: the phrase is hearted, relative to the word bid, which is also a synonym for tender.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender-hearted people are gentle and compassionate, which is kindly.

clue.text: Easy listening tunes, performed by 1 for the listener?

indicators.note: for the listener says the phrase is how it sounds, spelt another way

parts.note: the answer to 1 across is a cow, so its tunes would be music it lowed

explanation.surface: Light background music, played by the setter's first answer for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is a cow's name; music a cow mooed sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Background music meant to set an ambience is gentle, relaxing easy listening.
